title: test(formula): pin the refused direction of the hole placement scan's tag-open and script escape corrections (#25351)
body:
Closes #25351

The maintainer's action on #25351, written under the maintainer's delegation in chat: two refused-direction rows in the class-by-class refused table of `packages/formula/src/mail-html-hole-placement.test.ts`, one per scan correction of `86330c090` (PR #25212), as contract review `6342085020` ③ asked. Test-only: no change to the classifier, the rule, its doors or the renderer.

Per the card's disclosure rule, this body names each row by class only; the samples live in the test source.

## The two rows

1. **The tag-open state.** A hole inside a tag that opens immediately after a character the tag open state reconsumes in the data state answers `tag` and is refused.
2. **A script element's escape states.** A hole after an end tag in a script element's double-escaped text answers `raw-text-element` and is refused.

Both rows were built from the HTML Living Standard's tokenizer section (the tag open state; the script data escaped and double escaped states).

## Ablation (local, against the classifier at this PR's base)

Each correction of `86330c090` in `packages/formula/src/mail-html-hole-placement.ts` was reverted on its own, the file run, and the correction re-applied; the file was byte-identical to the base after each restore.

| Correction reverted | Rows red | Reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tag open state: reconsume in the data state (back to a plain return to data) | 1 of 48: the `tag` row added here | expected `tag`, received `element-text` |
| Script escape states: the escape flag's arm/disarm and the end-tag guard removed | 1 of 48: the `raw-text-element` row added here | expected `raw-text-element`, received `element-text` |

With both corrections in place: 48 of 48 pass in this file.
